leads.posting: Nutrition startup Ace Blend raises $9.91 Mn led by 3one4 Capital. Ace Blend, a nutrition startup, has raised $9.91 million in a Series A2 funding round led by 3one4 Capital, with existing investor Fireside Ventures doubling down on its investment. Fireside Ventures had previously led the company’s $3.3 million pre-Series A round. The fresh capital will support research-led product development and the launch of new nutrition formats. The company claims that it grew 300% in FY26, while more than 46% of its customers returned to make repeat purchases. Founded by Shivam Hingorani, Ace Blend began selling its products in 2018. Saif Mehkri joined as co-founder in 2022, bringing nearly three decades of experience in the nutrition industry. The company operates an integrated supply chain covering ingredient sourcing, formulation and manufacturing. Ace Blend develops nutritional products based on clinical evidence, focusing on nutrient forms, dosages and delivery methods. Its portfolio covers heart health, immunity, sleep, recovery and brain health. The company also works with global ingredient suppliers DSM and TCI, which have granted it exclusive rights in India to certain technologies. Its products are developed by an in-house clinical team and recommended by a network of more than 400 doctors. Clinical validation and automated testing are conducted independently by accredited laboratories in Europe. Ace Blend also holds issued patents for new nutrition formats designed for everyday use, with the first products expected to reach the market in the fourth quarter of FY27.

leads.posting: Docterz raises Rs 5 Cr from Vineeta Singh, Avnish Anand and 20 doctor-investors. Docterz, a healthcare technology startup founded by paediatrician Dr Atish Laddad, has raised Rs 5 crore from around 35 investors, including doctors who use its platform. Around 20 doctor users contributed nearly Rs 3 crore, accounting for about 60% of the total funding. The investor group also includes Vineeta Singh, co-founder and CEO of SUGAR Cosmetics, and Avnish Anand, co-founder and former CEO of CaratLane. The company plans to use the funds to expand organically, explore acquisitions and develop AI tools for doctors. It also aims to expand its reach among independent practitioners, smaller clinics and healthcare organisations across India. Founded over a decade ago, Docterz offers an integrated platform for electronic medical records, appointments, billing, vaccination management and patient engagement. Its technology supports more than 5,000 doctors across India, with a strong presence in paediatrics. The company is also developing AI-enabled tools to help doctors with documentation, administrative workflows, practice data analysis and patient follow-ups. Dr Dhananjay Sangle, a paediatrician and Docterz investor, said his decision to invest was based on his experience using the platform for several years and his confidence in its founder. Vineeta Singh said customer participation in a funding round was a strong signal for a business, adding that doctors investing in Docterz reflected their trust in the platform and its founder. Dr Suhas Warad, another paediatrician and investor in the company, said technology designed around doctors’ needs could help them manage their practices more efficiently and devote more time to patient care.

leads.posting: D2C apparel brand ReplyAll raises Rs 9.7 Cr in pre-Series A round. Direct-to-consumer (D2C) apparel brand ReplyAll has raised Rs 9.7 crore in pre-Series A funding round co-led by Sadev Ventures and Atom XVII. The round also saw participation from ISV and Long View Ventures, along with existing investors Sparrow and Antler, and a group of angel investors. The brand had previously secured Rs 6.8 crore ($750K) in its first funding round led by Sparrow Capital and Antler India, with participation from Bharat Founders Fund, DeVC, and several D2C founders in Dec. last year. The proceeds will be used to invest in fabric research and development, product design, new categories, and the brand’s retail and community presence, ReplyAll said in a press release. Launched in 2025 by Rushabh Sanghavi, ReplyAll offers performance wear and everyday apparel designed for work, travel, workouts and casual wear. The Bengaluru-based brand focuses on versatile styling, functional details and material innovation to develop clothing for everyday use. According to the company, its Temperform™ fabric, used in the Coolest Tee, is designed to help manage heat during everyday activities and sports. Its Flexknit™ material offers stretch and wrinkle resistance in trousers designed for work, travel and casual wear. ReplyAll plans to invest in further fabric research and expand its product categories. The company said it has recorded month-on-month revenue growth over the past seven months. Its first three product launches, the Coolest Tee, All-In Pants and Stepwise Tee, sold out, while repeat customers account for 40% of its revenue.
